newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE JUNE OIL PRODUCTS OUTPUT DOWN 5.4 PCT.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE JUNE OIL PRODUCTS OUTPUT DOWN 5.4 PCT.

text.p: Singapore's June petroleum products manufacturing output fell by 5.4 percent compared with the same month a year before, the Economic Development Board (EDB) said on Tuesday.

"Output of petroleum products declined by 5.4 percent as local refiners cut back production in the face of poor margins caused by an oversupply of capacity in regional refineries," the EDB said in a statement.
"Cumulative output for the first six months of 1997 was 7.8 percent less than in the same period in 1996," it said.
In late June, Shell Singapore, the island's largest refiner initiated a cut in output of about 15 percent at its 435,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery.

The cut in output is still being maintained but not at such a severe rate as margins have improved, a company spokeswoman told Reuters last week. She declined to reveal Shell's current operating rate.
Esso Singapore had also cut crude runs at its 230,000-bpd refinery in late June by about 10-percent, industry sources said. But a company spkeswoman declined to comment on the crude run cut.
EDB also said the petrochemicals industry continued to expand in June with the start up of the second chemical complex in late April.
"The June output increase of 70.9 percent led to the cumulative output increase of 39.1 percent for the first six months of 1997," it said.
